questions.q: According to this lesson, what should you show first when presenting your capstone in an interview or portfolio review?
options: A slide deck describing the project without showing the repository itself
The commit graph and branch history, proving a real feature branch was merged through a real pull request
An unrelated sample project instead of your own
The repository's README with no code or history shown
questions.explain: The lesson recommends starting with the commit graph and branch history because it visually proves the workflow is real, before discussing anything else.

questions.q: When discussing the pull request in your capstone, what does this lesson say you should specifically point to?
options: Only the final 'Approve' click, with no other detail
The description and an inline review comment you actually addressed with a follow-up commit
A pull request from someone else's unrelated repository
Nothing — pull requests aren't worth mentioning in an interview
questions.explain: Pointing at a real addressed review comment demonstrates you can both give and receive code review, not just click through approval.

questions.q: How should you answer 'What stops your deploy job from running on every single push?' according to this lesson?
options: By claiming deploy jobs can't be controlled at all
By explaining your own github.event_name and github.ref condition, in your own words, against your actual workflow file
By saying deploy jobs always run on every push with no way to prevent it
By avoiding the question entirely
questions.explain: The lesson ties this answer directly to Lesson 20's gating condition, now applied to the candidate's own real workflow file.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what was this course fundamentally about, beyond memorizing Git commands?
options: The actual mechanics of how software gets built, reviewed, integrated, and shipped safely on a team
Memorizing every Git command by name with no practical context
Avoiding collaboration with other developers entirely
Guaranteeing that merge conflicts never happen
questions.explain: The lesson frames the whole course around making team collaboration on shared code trustworthy and automatic, not dependent on individuals remembering to be careful.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what course comes next in the AI Engineer path after this one?
options: AI/ML Foundations
Python for AI Engineering
APIs & JSON for AI Applications
There is no next course — this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: This course is the second stop in the AI Engineer path, right after Python for AI Engineering, and is followed next by APIs & JSON for AI Applications.
